paragraphs.title: Thanksgiving and the Great Works of God

easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “Praise ye the LORD.”
He says, “I will praise the LORD with my whole heart.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist praise the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The works of the LORD are great.”
easy.q: How are the works of the LORD described?

answers: In the assembly of the upright and in the congregation
medium.explanation: He praises God “in the assembly of the upright, and in the congregation.”
medium.q: Where does the psalmist say he will praise the LORD?

medium.explanation: The LORD’s work is described as “honourable and glorious,” showing its majesty and excellence.
medium.q: What does “honourable and glorious” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “his righteousness endureth for ever.”
medium.q: What does “endureth for ever” show about the LORD’s righteousness?

answers: The works are great, and the work is majestic and righteous
The works are hidden, and righteousness is temporary
The works belong only to the upright
challenge.explanation: The verses join the greatness of God’s works with their honor, glory, and enduring righteousness.
challenge.q: What connection appears between verses 2 and 3?

challenge.explanation: “With my whole heart” describes wholehearted and sincere praise.
challenge.q: What does praising God “with my whole heart” emphasize?

answers: Praise of the LORD because of His great works and righteousness
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with praise and supports it by describing the greatness and righteousness of God’s works.
challenge.q: What is the main idea of verses 1–3?

paragraphs.title: The Remembrance of Wonders, the Covenant, and the Promise

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered.”
easy.q: What do the wonderful works of the LORD leave behind?

easy.explanation: The LORD “hath given meat unto them that fear him.”
easy.q: To whom does the LORD give meat?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “he will ever be mindful of his covenant.”
easy.q: What will the LORD always remember?

answers: Both show God’s care and faithfulness
Both describe the weakness of the people
medium.explanation: Giving meat and remembering the covenant show the LORD’s gracious and faithful care.
medium.q: How are the provision of food and the covenant related in this passage?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the inheritance of the heathen that God gives to His people.
medium.q: What does “the heritage of the heathen” mean in this context?

answers: Remembrance of wonders, care for those who fear God, remembrance of the covenant, revelation of His power, and the promised inheritance
The inheritance first, then praise, and finally remembrance
Fear of the LORD, wisdom, and then judgment
medium.explanation: The passage moves from remembered wonders and provision to the covenant, God’s power, and the inheritance He gives.
medium.q: What is the main sequence of ideas in verses 4–6?

answers: Both show that the wonders and covenant remain continually remembered
The first concerns the future and the second erases the past
The first describes food and the second describes praise
challenge.explanation: Both expressions emphasize lasting remembrance of God’s wonders and covenant.
challenge.q: What connection is there between “remembered” in verse 4 and “mindful” in verse 5?

answers: The power of His works and the inheritance He will give
The names of all the nations
challenge.explanation: He “hath shewed his people the power of his works” so that He may give them the heritage of the heathen.
challenge.q: What does the LORD show His people according to this passage?

answers: The covenant is remembered and fulfilled through God’s works
challenge.explanation: God remembers His covenant and demonstrates His power in giving the promised inheritance.
challenge.q: How is the promise related to the covenant?

paragraphs.title: The Trustworthiness of the Works, Redemption, and Fear of God

easy.explanation: His works are “verity and judgment,” and “all his commandments are sure.”
easy.q: How are the works of the LORD and His commandments described?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He sent redemption unto his people.”
easy.q: What did the LORD send to His people?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.”
easy.q: What is the fear of the LORD called in the final verse?

answers: They are hidden for a short time
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the lasting stability of God’s works.
medium.q: What does “They stand fast for ever and ever” mean about God’s works?

answers: His holy and reverend name leads to fear of the LORD
His name removes the need for fear
Fear causes His name to disappear
medium.explanation: The passage calls His name “holy and reverend” and then presents the fear of the LORD as the beginning of wisdom.
medium.q: What connection is made between God’s name and the fear of the LORD?

answers: Redemption is sent, and the covenant is commanded forever
medium.explanation: The verse mentions both that God “sent redemption” and that He “hath commanded his covenant for ever.”
medium.q: How are redemption and the covenant related in this passage?

answers: They show that God’s works and commandments are trustworthy
They show that the commandments are temporary
They completely separate God’s works from His commandments
challenge.explanation: Truth, judgment, and certainty together show that God’s works and commandments can be trusted.
challenge.q: What connection is there between “verity and judgment” and “sure”?

answers: The fear of the LORD prevents all action
The fear of the LORD has no connection with wisdom
The fear of the LORD is a foundation for wisdom and sound understanding
challenge.explanation: The verse calls the fear of the LORD the beginning of wisdom and gives good understanding to those who do His commandments.
challenge.q: What is implied by the connection between the fear of the LORD and “a good understanding”?

answers: To all who do His commandments
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.”
challenge.q: To whom is “a good understanding” given at the end of the psalm?
